arxiv-2208.03699.heading: Multi-Modal Formal Modeling Language for Hardware & Systems
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2208.03699.text: UCLID5 is a formal modeling, verification, and synthesis framework and specification language designed for heterogeneous hardware and software systems. It enables compositional specification of Register-Transfer Level (RTL) datapaths, control logic, memory subsystems, and security monitors using first-order and temporal logic assertions.

arxiv-2208.03699.heading: Bridging Chisel, FIRRTL, and SMT Solvers
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2208.03699.text: In semiconductor design workflows, UCLID5 integrates with modern hardware construction languages such as Chisel and FIRRTL as well as SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA). Models are lowered to Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers and syntax-guided synthesis (SyGuS) engines for bounded model checking, inductive invariant synthesis, and hyperproperty verification.

arxiv-2208.03699.heading: Verification of Secure Architectures and Accelerators
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2208.03699.text: UCLID5 has been deployed to formally verify speculative execution mitigations, cryptographic accelerators, enclave isolation, and hardware fault-tolerance protocols prior to silicon tapeout.

arxiv-2503.19174.heading: Bottlenecks in Writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVAs)
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2503.19174.text: Formal Property Verification (FPV) in chip and semiconductor design relies heavily on SystemVerilog Assertions (SVAs) and Property Specification Language (PSL) to mathematically prove that Register-Transfer Level (RTL) implementations satisfy architectural specifications. Writing temporal logic assertions manually is error-prone and requires deep verification expertise.

arxiv-2503.19174.heading: Unified Specification-and-RTL Knowledge Graph
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2503.19174.text: AssertionForge constructs a unified hardware Knowledge Graph (KG) that fuses natural-language specification requirements with structural RTL signal interactions, finite-state machines, and clock/reset domains. Multi-resolution context retrieval over this graph prevents signal hallucination during automated SVA synthesis.

arxiv-2503.19174.heading: Formal Property Verification Closure
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2503.19174.text: Evaluated across industrial semiconductor IP blocks using commercial EDA formal verification engines, AssertionForge substantially increases syntax validity, temporal accuracy, and cone-of-influence coverage compared to baseline Large Language Model assertion generators.

arxiv-2604.23100.heading: Solver-in-the-Loop Formal Assertion Synthesis
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2604.23100.text: ProofLoop introduces a two-phase agentic framework that bridges natural-language hardware specifications, Register-Transfer Level (RTL) abstract syntax trees (ASTs), and formal verification languages such as SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA).

arxiv-2604.23100.heading: Iterative Refinement with EDA Proof Engines
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
arxiv-2604.23100.text: In Phase A, ProofLoop queries an AST-indexed structural representation of the Verilog/SystemVerilog design to ground clock, reset, and handshake signals. In Phase B, a solver-in-the-loop agent invokes commercial formal verification engines such as Cadence JasperGold, parses counterexample traces and vacuity reports, and iteratively repairs candidate SVA properties until mathematical proof closure is achieved.

arxiv-2604.23100.heading: Implications for Semiconductor Verification Flows
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2604.23100.text: Coupling deterministic formal solvers with automated assertion synthesis eliminates vacuous properties and accelerates pre-silicon verification of complex SoC interconnects and AI accelerator datapaths.

arxiv-2609.26751.heading: Behavioral Equivalence in Hardware Verification Languages
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2609.26751.text: Evaluating automated SystemVerilog Assertion (SVA) generators requires distinguishing true behavioral temporal properties from brittle assertions tied to incidental RTL coding style. EquivSVA provides a formally verified benchmark organized around behavior families of structurally distinct RTL implementations sharing identical interface specifications.

arxiv-2609.26751.heading: Formal Equivalence & Metamorphic Verification
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2609.26751.text: Every gold SVA assertion in EquivSVA is mechanically verified using formal property verification (FPV) and SMT-based equivalence checking across pipelined, FSM-encoded, and Chisel/FIRRTL-generated RTL variants.

arxiv-2609.26751.heading: Advancing Robust Semiconductor Verification
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
arxiv-2609.26751.text: EquivSVA enables rigorous benchmarking of formal verification language translators, theorem-proving hardware frameworks (Kami, Coq), and LLM-assisted assertion synthesis pipelines.

arxiv-2610.08739v2.heading: Problem Statement: Bit-Flip Vulnerability in DNNs
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
arxiv-2610.08739v2.text: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are integral to many safety critical systems, yet they remain highly vulnerable to bit-flip attacks (BFAs), where a few memory level perturbations can drastically degrade accuracy. Existing defenses incur significant hardware overhead, depend on retraining, or fail against targeted flips.

arxiv-2610.08739v2.heading: BARE-AI Architecture: APCs and PULSE
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
arxiv-2610.08739v2.text: We propose BARE-AI, a runtime framework that detects, localizes, and mitigates BFAs during inference. BARE-AI introduces AI Performance Counters (APCs), lightweight hardware monitors in the accelerator datapath that capture per-layer activation statistics such as sparsity, entropy, kurtosis, and spectral shift. These are analyzed by the Predictive Unit for Layer Security Evaluation (PULSE), a compact detector trained offline as an ensemble of classifiers and realized on-chip as a small neural engine.

arxiv-2610.08739v2.heading: Fault Localization and Weight Recovery
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
arxiv-2610.08739v2.text: For explainability and recovery, BARE-AI introduces an Activation Shift Index (ASI) for layer level fault localization and a z-score based repair that resets anomalous weights toward clean layer statistics.

arxiv-2610.08739v2.heading: Evaluation Across CNNs, ViTs, and LLMs
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
arxiv-2610.08739v2.text: Across CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Large Language Models under random, targeted, adaptive, and magnitude based BFAs, BARE-AI achieves up to 98% detection accuracy on vision models and 74% to 95% on language models, restores near clean accuracy for CNNs and ViTs, and provides partial recovery for LLMs.

arxiv-2610.08739v2.heading: Hardware Overhead at 28nm
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
arxiv-2610.08739v2.text: Synthesized at 28nm, the monitoring infrastructure incurs under 3% energy, under 4% area, and about 10% latency overhead, with a configurable operating point that reduces latency overhead to about 6%. Unlike error correcting codes, whose redundancy grows with the number of tolerated flips, BARE-AI's overhead remains constant regardless of attack strength, making it attractive for resource constrained, safety critical edge applications such as autonomous systems, energy, and healthcare.

arxiv-2610.33748.heading: Fil-C Software Capabilities & Hardware Assumptions
taxonomy_paths: Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2610.33748.text: Fil-C retrofits spatial and temporal memory safety onto C and C++ programs using software capabilities (InvisiCaps) checked on every pointer dereference. However, Fil-C relies on an unstated hardware assumption that DRAM reliably preserves capability metadata. In Fil-C, each heap pointer's upper-bound word is stored inline in ordinary DRAM without hardware integrity protection.

arxiv-2610.33748.heading: Rowhammer Bit-Flip Attack Mechanism
taxonomy_paths: Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
arxiv-2610.33748.text: A single 0-to-1 bit-flip induced by Rowhammer in a pointer's upper-bound metadata expands the pointer's permitted memory range by 2^k bytes. Because the runtime treats the corrupted upper bound as authoritative, it silently permits out-of-bounds reads and writes without raising any panic, signal, or exception.

arxiv-2610.33748.heading: End-to-End Evaluation on DDR3 and DDR4 with TRR
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
arxiv-2610.33748.text: Using both a deterministic fault-injection model and physical end-to-end Rowhammer reproduction on DDR3 and DDR4 memory equipped with Target Row Refresh (TRR), the authors demonstrate bounded read/write windows, secret disclosure, privilege escalation, and multi-tenant SQLite API key leakage, along with a probabilistic small-step operational semantics for memory fault reasoning.

note-2026-cross-layer-bitflip-synthesis.heading: Unifying Hardware Datapath Telemetry and Software Capability Integrity
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
note-2026-cross-layer-bitflip-synthesis.text: Both BARE-AI (arXiv:2610.08739v2) and the Fil-C Rowhammer study (arXiv:2610.33748) expose a critical cross-layer insight: neither Deep Neural Network weights nor language-level software capabilities (InvisiCaps) can assume uncorrupted DRAM when subjected to targeted bit-flip attacks.

note-2026-cross-layer-bitflip-synthesis.heading: OntoLogic Knowledge Graph Synthesis
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
note-2026-cross-layer-bitflip-synthesis.text: In our conceptual taxonomy, Bit-Flip Attacks bridge Hardware & Semiconductor Systems (AI Accelerators, Memory & Interconnects) and Security & Resilience (Memory Safety & Software Capabilities, Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery). Lightweight on-chip monitors (APCs, PULSE, ASI) and z-score statistical repair provide constant-overhead mitigation where traditional ECC or DDR4 Target Row Refresh (TRR) fall short.

research-formal-verification-languages-i.heading: Research Scope & Core Languages: Formal verification languages in chip and semiconductor design
taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
research-formal-verification-languages-i.text: In chip and semiconductor design, Formal Verification Languages provide the mathematical foundation for specifying and proving Register-Transfer Level (RTL) and architectural invariants before silicon fabrication. The industrial backbone comprises IEEE 1800 SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) and IEEE 1850 Property Specification Language (PSL) for linear temporal logic (LTL) Formal Property Verification (FPV), complemented by multi-modal verification and hardware construction languages including UCLID5 (SMT-backed datapath/control modeling), Chisel/FIRRTL (ChiselFV), and Coq-embedded theorem-proving frameworks such as Kami.

research-formal-verification-languages-i.heading: Knowledge-Graph & Solver-in-the-Loop Assertion Synthesis
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification > Formal Verification Languages & Assertions
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
research-formal-verification-languages-i.text: Recent research synthesized in this collection — UCLID5: Multi-Modal Formal Modeling, Verification, and Synthesis (arxiv-2208.03699); AssertionForge: Enhancing Formal Verification Assertion Generation with Structured Representation of Specifications and RTL (arxiv-2503.19174); ProofLoop: From Language to Logic — Bridging LLMs and Formal Representations for RTL Assertion Generation (arxiv-2604.23100); EquivSVA: A Formally Verified Dataset of Behavioral Assertions Across Equivalent RTL Implementations (arxiv-2609.26751) — addresses the manual bottleneck of authoring temporal logic assertions. Frameworks like AssertionForge construct unified Knowledge Graphs fusing natural-language specs and RTL structure, while agentic solver-in-the-loop systems like ProofLoop interact directly with commercial EDA formal engines (Cadence JasperGold and SMT solvers) to iteratively refine SVA assertions until formal proof closure.

research-formal-verification-languages-i.heading: Cross-Layer Integration with Hardware Telemetry & Security
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks

Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
research-formal-verification-languages-i.text: Within our OntoLogic-ready knowledge graph, formal verification languages connect pre-silicon EDA verification with runtime hardware security monitors (such as BARE-AI's 28nm AI Performance Counters and PULSE neural detectors) and probabilistic operational semantics for memory-level bit-flip resilience (such as Rowhammer analysis on Fil-C software capabilities).

taxonomy_paths: Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification

techpaper-2026-eda-formal-monitors.text: Hardware performance monitors such as AI Performance Counters (APCs) and on-chip neural detectors like PULSE must themselves be verified against fault injection and timing side channels during RTL synthesis and place and route.

techpaper-2026-eda-formal-monitors.heading: Operational Semantics and Pre-Silicon Fault Simulation
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > EDA & Hardware Verification
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
techpaper-2026-eda-formal-monitors.text: By combining formal verification at the 28nm RTL boundary with probabilistic operational semantics for memory-level bit-flip perturbations, EDA toolflows can certify layer-level fault localization bounds prior to tapeout.

techpaper-2026-hbm-chiplet-resilience.heading: High-Bandwidth Memory & Chiplet Interconnect Threat Surface
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Security & Resilience > Hardware Fault Attacks > Bit-Flip Attacks
Security & Resilience > Runtime Fault Localization & Recovery
techpaper-2026-hbm-chiplet-resilience.text: Modern AI accelerators increasingly pair HBM3 and CXL memory subsystems with multi-die UCIe chiplet architectures. While error correcting codes (ECC) and Target Row Refresh (TRR) mitigate single-bit random faults, concentrated Rowhammer and targeted bit-flip attacks across shared memory channels threaten both Vision Transformers and Large Language Models.

techpaper-2026-hbm-chiplet-resilience.heading: Co-Design of Memory Telemetry and Datapath Monitors
taxonomy_paths: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning > Deep Neural Networks
Hardware & Semiconductor Systems > AI Accelerators > Built-in Performance Monitors
Security & Resilience > Memory Safety & Software Capabilities
techpaper-2026-hbm-chiplet-resilience.text: Combining inline memory controller telemetry with datapath AI Performance Counters (APCs) enables early anomaly detection before corrupted weights or pointer capability metadata propagate across UCIe die-to-die links.
